# Accent color and gray tone

**HabitForge lets you choose one of 26 accent colors and one of six gray tones, and that pair colors the entire app — the accent paints buttons, links, focus rings, selected states, and the loading logo, while the gray sets page backgrounds, card surfaces, and borders.** Both are part of the [theme customizer](./customizer) and use color-swatch selectors with a check mark on the active choice, not dropdown menus. Defaults are **Indigo** accent and **Slate** gray. The colors come from the Radix color system, so each one is engineered for readable contrast in both light and dark appearance. Everything here is free — there are no locked or premium colors.

## Use cases

### Personalizing the app to feel like yours

A habit app is something you open every day, so the look matters. Picking an accent you like — jade, violet, tomato, gold, or any of the rest — makes the daily check-in feel a little more rewarding. The accent is intentionally everywhere, so one choice re-themes the whole experience.

### Keeping contrast comfortable

The gray tone changes the "temperature" of the neutral surfaces. Slate is cool and crisp; sand and olive are warmer and softer on the eyes. If a cool gray feels stark in dark mode, switching to mauve or sage takes the edge off without touching your accent.

### Color-coding by context

Some users keep a calm blue or sky accent for focus and a warmer amber or orange when they want the app to feel more energetic. Because the change is instant and free to flip as often as you like, you can treat the accent as a mood dial.

## The full palette

**Accent colors (26):** tomato, red, ruby, crimson, pink, plum, purple, violet, iris, indigo, blue, cyan, teal, jade, green, grass, bronze, gold, brown, orange, amber, yellow, lime, mint, sky, and gray.

**Gray tones (6):** gray, mauve, slate, sage, olive, and sand.

The accent swatches are laid out as a responsive grid; the gray swatches as a compact row. Hover or focus a swatch to see its name in a tooltip, and the selected swatch carries a check mark.

## How to change your colors

1. Open the **theme customizer** from the **palette icon** in the header.
2. Under **Accent Color**, tap any swatch. A check mark appears and the whole app recolors instantly.
3. Under **Gray Color**, tap a tone (Gray, Mauve, Slate, Sage, Olive, or Sand) to set the neutral surfaces.
4. Glance at the buttons and headings behind the dialog to confirm the combination reads well, then close the dialog.

There is no separate save step — each tap is applied immediately and stored the same way as the rest of your theme.

## Accent and gray work together

The accent and gray are designed to be paired. A cool accent (blue, indigo, iris) sits naturally on slate or gray; a warm accent (amber, orange, gold, bronze) often looks better on sand or olive. There is no wrong combination — both layers stay legible because each Radix color ships with tuned contrast steps for text, borders, and backgrounds in light and dark modes.

If you set **Panel Background** to **Translucent** in the [customizer](./customizer), a faint wash of your accent shows through card surfaces, tying the accent and gray together even more. On **Solid**, panels stay fully opaque and the gray tone leads.

## Tips

- **Choose the accent first, then the gray.** The accent is the loud layer; pick it, then settle the neutral around it.
- **Check both appearances.** A pair that sings in light mode can feel different in dark — flip [appearance](./customizer) once to confirm.
- **Warm accent, warm gray.** Pair amber/orange/gold with sand or olive; pair blue/indigo/iris with slate or gray for the most natural look.
- **Subtle beats loud for all-day use.** Very saturated accents are great for short bursts but can tire the eye over long sessions.

## FAQ

### Does the accent color change anything besides looks?

No. It is purely visual. Buttons, links, focus outlines, selected cards, and the loading logo adopt the accent, but no behavior or data changes.

### Will my color choices sync to my other devices?

Yes, when you are signed in. Accent and gray are stored with your account theme settings and pulled on your other devices. Signed out, they stay on the current device. See [Cross-device sync](./sync).

### Why are some colors so similar (red, ruby, crimson)?

They are distinct Radix hues with slightly different undertones. The variety lets you fine-tune the exact shade rather than settle for one generic "red."

### Are any colors paid or locked?

No. All 26 accents and all six gray tones are free.

### Do these colors meet contrast guidelines?

The Radix color scales are built for accessible contrast across their steps. HabitForge's [accessibility statement](https://habitforge.aoneahsan.com) targets WCAG 2.1 AA for text and UI contrast.
